headline: Five stripes a side: Glickman's 1970 pinwheel still carries Portland's look.
summary: The Blazers run one of the league's most disciplined identities: red, black and white, under a pinwheel of two sets of five stripes that has been redrawn but never replaced. Fans dress by era, from Walton's 1977 whites to Lillard's red "Rip City". City Editions keep circling plaid and carpet, and this season brings no new one, just a 2019-20 re-wear. The untold material is the Coliseum, lower Albina, Vanport and Portland's double design birthright: the pinwheel in 1970 and the Swoosh in 1971.

insights.title: A heritage gap in a heritage year
insights.detail: Portland is re-wearing its 2019-20 City Edition in 2026-27 and wasn't among the eight franchises in Nike's Specter program. Yet this is the 50th-anniversary season of the 1976-77 title, clinched June 5, 1977 at Memorial Coliseum.
insights.implication: Lead the season with a '77-at-50 capsule: a warmup, a shooting shirt and a patch, plus a Classic Edition proposal if the team and league agree. The anniversary needs product before the playoffs.

insights.title: The pinwheel is a stripe system
insights.detail: Glickman's 1970 mark is two interlocking sets of five stripes, one for each team of five on the floor. Fans simply call it "the pinwheel". Redraws in the early 1990s, 2002 and 2017 changed the angle and the trim but kept the five-and-five logic.
insights.implication: Build trims, taping and knit patterns from five-plus-five stripes instead of adding new marks. It reads as Blazers from across a room, even without a logo.

insights.title: Fans dress by era, and the diagonal is the one they miss
insights.detail: Lifers wear 1977 Walton and Lucas, the Drexler, Porter and Kersey teams with the shoulder-to-hip red-and-black slash, Roy's #7 black "Portland", and Lillard's #0 red "Rip City". Mitchell & Ness largely owns vintage replicas.
insights.implication: Nike's lane is new-cut product that revives the diagonal slash, such as warmups, shooting shirts and a modern Statement or Classic treatment. Don't compete on straight replicas.

insights.title: Plaid and carpet are tapped out
insights.detail: Four straight City Editions have run on two motifs. The PDX carpet came in 2022-23. Dr. Jack plaid, honoring Jack Ramsay's loud sport coats, followed in 2023-24, then an all-over plaid in 2024-25 and a return to the carpet in 2025-26.
insights.implication: Open a fresh vein with the next new City Edition: Coliseum glass, Albina, radio-era "Rip City" or the 1970-71 design origin story. Keep plaid and carpet as linings and accents only.

insights.title: Two homecomings, two brands
insights.detail: Lillard returns from his Achilles tear for his first Blazers home games since 2023. Morant, a Nike signature athlete, debuts in Portland. Lillard is a longtime adidas signature athlete.
insights.implication: Stock deep in Lillard and Morant Swingmans across Association, Icon, Statement and the re-worn City Edition for the home opener and the Oct 30 Cup night against Golden State. Tell the player-exclusive story through Morant's Ja line.

insights.title: 'Rip City' is a radio call, not a slogan
insights.detail: Broadcaster Bill Schonely shouted "Rip City! All right!" after a Jim Barnett long jumper against the Lakers in the 1970-71 season. The phrase now sits on jerseys and courts. His voice, his other calls and the transistor-radio era that spread them have never been the design.
insights.implication: A broadcast-era treatment of "Rip City!" (call-sign lettering, the exclamation mark, a dial graphic) gives the mark a fresh, Portland-only story without inventing anything new.

places.name: Veterans Memorial Coliseum
places.why: The SOM glass-box arena (1960) where the Blazers played from 1970 to 1995, won the 1977 title and began the 814-game sellout streak. It was built on land cleared of Black homes and businesses.

places.name: Moda Center
places.why: The home since 1995, still called "the Rose Garden" by many fans. A publicly funded renovation is about to start and will reset the in-arena brand canvas.

places.name: Portland International Airport (PDX)
places.why: Source of the teal 1987 carpet that carried two City Editions. Its new mass-timber terminal is the city's newest civic design statement.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee
places.why: A sneaker-culture coffee shop founded by former Nike employee Ian Williams, where Portland's sneaker crowd gathers and drops get talked about. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

places.name: Matt Dishman Community Center
places.why: A historic gym in the heart of Black Albina, and the natural partner venue for any Albina-rooted uniform or court story.

places.name: Irving Park courts
places.why: Northeast Portland's best-known outdoor pickup run, where local players will judge what Blazers gear actually looks good on a court.

places.name: Oregon Historical Society
places.why: The archive for Vanport, Albina, Coliseum and early-Blazers photography, and the place to research any heritage graphic before using it.

places.name: Vanport site (Delta Park / Portland International Raceway)
places.why: The site of the wartime city erased by the May 30, 1948 flood. Its displaced Black residents reshaped Albina.

people.name: Frank Glickman
people.role: Boston graphic artist and cousin of founder Harry Glickman; designed the 1970 pinwheel logo
people.why: The author of the franchise's one enduring mark. Crediting him by name gives heritage product an origin story beyond "retro".

people.name: Bill Schonely
people.why: He coined "Rip City" in the team's first season, so every Rip City wordmark is his call.

people.name: Bill Walton
people.role: 1977 Finals MVP and Hall of Famer (died 2024)
people.why: The face of the title's 50th anniversary. His Deadhead tie-dye persona is beloved, but the Grateful Dead marks belong to someone else.

people.name: Clyde Drexler
people.why: "Clyde the Glide" in the diagonal-stripe uniform of the 1990 and 1992 Finals is the era Portland's forty- and fifty-something fans dress in.

people.name: Damian Lillard
people.role: All-time franchise scoring leader, back from an Achilles tear
people.why: His #0 is the most-worn modern Blazers jersey, and his return is the season's emotional jersey moment. His own marks run through adidas.

people.name: Carolyn Davidson
people.role: Designer of the Nike Swoosh (1971), then a Portland State University design student
people.why: With Glickman's pinwheel a year earlier, she makes Portland the birthplace of two of sport's best-known marks. Only this city has that design story.

people.name: Albina Vision Trust
people.role: Black-led nonprofit planning to rebuild lower Albina around the Rose Quarter
people.why: The rightful co-author of any Coliseum or Albina uniform story, since its work is on the same land the arenas sit on.

people.name: Portland Gear (Marcus Harvey)
people.why: Proof that a plain "Portland" wordmark sells. It shows the local appetite for city-first, not logo-first, product.

moments.name: Home opener and Lillard's first home game back
moments.why: The biggest jersey-buying night of the season: Lillard's homecoming and Morant's Moda Center debut.

moments.name: NBA Cup Night: Warriors at Trail Blazers
moments.why: The opening Cup game, at home against Golden State, is a national-window chance to show the season's product early.

moments.name: Black History Month
moments.why: A natural window for an Albina- or Vanport-rooted product, but only as part of a year-round partnership, not a one-off.

moments.name: Vanport flood anniversary and Vanport Mosaic Festival
moments.timing: Around Memorial Day; the flood was May 30, 1948
moments.why: The community-led commemoration of the event that shaped Black Portland, and the place to co-develop and launch a Vanport story.

moments.name: Rose Festival Grand Floral Parade
moments.why: The Rose City's own pageant falls during the playoffs and the '77 anniversary week: a ready-made street audience for heritage product.

moments.name: 1977 championship 50th anniversary
moments.why: Fifty years to the day since the Game 6 win over Philadelphia at the Coliseum. It's the date for a '77 capsule drop and a Blazermania revival.

vocabulary.meaning: Schonely's 1971 call, now the city's nickname and the team's second wordmark.
Fans' name for the five-and-five stripe logo.
The citywide fever of the 1977 title run, shorthand for peak Portland fandom.
Bill Schonely's nickname, used affectionately by generations of radio listeners.
Plaid named for 1977 title coach Jack Ramsay's loud sport coats, and the theme of the 2023-24 City Edition.
The arena's 1995-2013 name, which many fans still use for the Moda Center.
The 814 straight home sellouts from 1977 to 1995, a point of pride for older fans.
The teal PDX airport carpet, a local meme turned merch staple and twice a City Edition.

designCues.cue: Pinwheel red, used exactly to the NBA spec as the signal color on black or white grounds.
designCues.source: Official Blazers red, used since 1970 on the pinwheel and the 'Rip City' alternate.
designCues.use: Use it as the hit (stripes, numbers, a single zip or hood lining), not a full red base, so it stays a signal.

designCues.cue: True black base, the color of the Roy- and Lillard-era 'Portland' road and Icon jerseys.
designCues.source: Official Blazers black, the base of the Icon jersey and most fan outerwear.
designCues.use: Use as the ground for outerwear and lifestyle pieces, with red and white kept to stripe-width details.

designCues.cue: Five-and-five: two interlocking sets of five stripes, one per team of five, taken from the pinwheel and used as a trim system.
designCues.source: Frank Glickman's 1970 logo and its later redraws.
designCues.use: Use as five-stripe side taping, collar ribs, waistband jacquard or a knit hat cuff. Never stretch it to more or fewer than five.

designCues.cue: The diagonal slash: a shoulder-to-hip red-and-black stripe band across the chest.
designCues.source: The Blazers' home and road jerseys of the late 1970s to early 2000s, including the 1990 and 1992 Finals teams.
designCues.use: Use on warmups, shooting shirts and a modern Classic or Statement treatment for fans who dress in the Drexler era.

designCues.cue: Coliseum curtain wall: the tall glass-and-mullion grid around Memorial Coliseum's bowl, which glows at night.
designCues.source: Veterans Memorial Coliseum (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, 1960), home of the 1977 title and the 814 sellouts.
designCues.use: Use as a woven jacquard or sublimated side panel, only within a story co-authored with Albina partners that acknowledges whose homes were cleared for the building.

designCues.cue: Broadcast-era 'Rip City!': call-sign lettering with the exclamation mark kept, plus a radio-dial graphic.
designCues.source: Schonely's 1971 call and the radio broadcasts that built Blazermania.
designCues.use: Use on a pregame tee, a jock tag reading "All right!" or a shooting-shirt back. These are team marks, so no outside license is needed.

designCues.cue: Waffle grid: the Bowerman waffle-sole pattern as a texture.
designCues.source: Nike's own Oregon origin story from the same years as the pinwheel and 'Rip City'.
designCues.use: Use as a debossed waistband, embossed jock tag or knit texture. It ties Nike to the Blazers' founding years without putting a Swoosh on the chest.

productHooks: '77 at 50 capsule: a Walton-era white warmup, a shooting shirt with a 1977-2027 patch and a proposed 1976-77 Classic Edition if the team and league agree. Release it at the home opener, with a second drop on June 5, 2027.

Homecoming and debut jerseys: deep Lillard #0 and Morant Swingman stock in all four editions, including the re-worn 2019-20 City, for the home opener and the Oct 30 Cup night. Add a Blazers player exclusive of Morant's Ja shoe.
Diagonal collection: a full-zip warmup, shooting shirt and mesh short with the shoulder-to-hip slash and five-and-five taping. Aim it at the Drexler-era fan and release it before a Lakers home date.

Next new City Edition brief, "Lower Albina": the Coliseum curtain-wall grid and Albina's history, co-designed and paid through Albina Vision Trust and Black Portland artists. Proceeds are committed to the neighborhood, and the launch happens in Albina at a partner venue.
"Two Marks" design-history tee and hoodie: Glickman's 1970 pinwheel and Davidson's 1971 Swoosh told as Portland's design birthright, with proceeds to a Portland State design scholarship.
watchouts: Third-party IP needs clearance or avoidance. That covers the PDX carpet (Port of Portland), Pendleton-style plaid, Grateful Dead imagery around Walton and Taco Bell's "Cha-lu-pa!" chant. It also covers Lillard's personal marks, "Dame Time" and "Dame D.O.L.L.A.", since he is an adidas athlete.

The "Trail Blazers" name evokes Oregon Trail settlers. Skip wagon and pioneer nostalgia and never use Native imagery. Route any Indigenous theme through Portland Native partners such as NAYA, credited and paid, with no sacred or ceremonial designs.

Coliseum and Rose Quarter nostalgia sits on land cleared of Black Albina homes and businesses. Any arena-heritage product has to carry that truth, co-authored with Albina partners and not as a February one-off.
Morant's 2023 NBA suspensions over firearm videos mean his debut product should be basketball-first, with no weapon-adjacent or "outlaw" framing. Launch roster-wide, not around one player.
Don't glamorize the early-2000s "Jail Blazers" era, and don't ship a fifth plaid or carpet story. Locals will read it as recycled.

eras.look: Glickman's original pinwheel in red, black and white on white home and red road jerseys, worn by the expansion team and then by Walton, Lucas and Ramsay's 1977 champions.
eras.legacy: The title uniform and the root of Blazermania, and the most-wanted throwback of the 50th-anniversary season.

eras.look: The shoulder-to-hip red-and-black diagonal slash on white 'Blazers' home and dark 'Portland' road jerseys, with the pinwheel tilted in the early-1990s redraw.
eras.legacy: The Drexler, Porter and Kersey Finals teams of 1990 and 1992 and the 2000 West finalists. Apart from the "Jail Blazers" years, it's the era fans most often dress in.

eras.look: A silver-trimmed redraw of the pinwheel, white 'Blazers' and black 'Portland', and a red 'Rip City' alternate in the 2010s.
eras.legacy: The Roy, Aldridge and early-Lillard years. Roy's #7 black and Lillard's red "Rip City" are cult favorites.

eras.look: Nike's Association, Icon and Statement set with a streamlined pinwheel, plus annual City Editions that recently cycled between the PDX carpet and plaid.
eras.legacy: Clean core uniforms, but City Editions that locals see as stuck on two motifs. 2026-27 re-wears the 2019-20 City design.

cityEditions.concept: A re-wear of the 2019-20 City Edition, from the franchise's 50th season, rather than a new design.
cityEditions.note: Its design and story need confirming. With no new City story, there's room for heritage product.

cityEditions.concept: A return to the teal PDX airport carpet.
cityEditions.note: The carpet sells as a meme, but a second carpet uniform in four seasons fed the "tapped out" read.

cityEditions.concept: An all-over plaid uniform, reportedly with Mt. Hood references.
cityEditions.note: The second straight plaid. Check fan and sales response before any plaid follow-up.

cityEditions.concept: 'Dr. Jack' plaid honoring 1977 title coach Jack Ramsay's loud sport coats.
cityEditions.note: A true insider tribute to the title coach. How fans received it needs a live check.

cityEditions.concept: The teal 1987 PDX airport carpet pattern, the city's favorite meme.
cityEditions.note: The carpet is beloved local kitsch, and the team's return to it in 2025-26 suggests it sold. Confirm with sales data.

cityEditions.concept: The franchise's 50th-season City Edition, being re-worn in 2026-27.
cityEditions.note: Design details aren't confirmed in this draft.

fanFavorites: The 1976-77 Walton and Lucas title-season whites
Drexler-era diagonal-slash jerseys from the 1990 and 1992 Finals runs, white 'Blazers' or dark 'Portland'
Lillard #0 in the red 'Rip City' alternate

untoldStories.story: Lower Albina and the Coliseum: the Black neighborhood cleared for Memorial Coliseum and I-5 in the 1950s and 60s, now the focus of Albina Vision Trust's plan to rebuild.
untoldStories.why: It's literally the ground the franchise was born on. Telling it with Albina partners, during a public-money arena renovation, would make the most meaningful uniform in team history.

untoldStories.story: Vanport, 1942-1948: Oregon's wartime boomtown, erased by the May 30, 1948 flood, whose displaced Black families were pushed into Albina by redlining.
untoldStories.why: Few Portlanders outside North and Northeast know it. Told with the Vanport Mosaic community, it explains how Black Portland and its basketball culture formed.

untoldStories.story: Rip City as a voice: Schonely's 1971 call and the transistor-radio Blazermania that spread it.
untoldStories.why: Every fan uses the phrase, but few know its sound and origin. A broadcast-era treatment honors the Schonz without inventing a new slogan.

untoldStories.story: Two marks, one city: Glickman's pinwheel in 1970 and PSU student Carolyn Davidson's Swoosh in 1971.
untoldStories.why: Only Portland can claim both. It frames the Nike-Blazers relationship as shared civic design history, not a sponsorship.

untoldStories.story: The 814: 18 years of straight home sellouts from 1977 to 1995, in a glass-walled Coliseum and then the Rose Garden.
untoldStories.why: It celebrates the fans, not a player, which suits a city that sees itself as the league's most loyal small market.

verify: The design, concept and game schedule of the 2019-20 City Edition being re-worn in 2026-27 (this draft could not recall its design).

City Edition history and fan reception: PDX carpet 2022-23, Dr. Jack plaid 2023-24, all-over plaid with Mt. Hood references 2024-25, carpet return 2025-26, plus the 2017-18, 2018-19, 2020-21 and 2021-22 designs this draft leaves out.
Whether the Blazers or the NBA plan a 1977 title 50th-anniversary program in 2026-27 (Classic Edition, patch, June 5, 2027 event), and which Classic Editions Portland has worn under Nike.
Lillard's and Morant's 2026-27 jersey numbers, Lillard's current adidas contract, and the current Nike Ja signature model and release calendar.
The current Association, Icon and Statement designs (including the Statement wordmark) and whether the Dundon ownership plans any identity or uniform change.
The 2026-27 home-opener date and the Lakers home dates.
Rights to the PDX carpet pattern (Port of Portland) and the licensing route for any carpet or plaid reference.
That Deadstock Coffee and the Irving Park courts are operating as described in 2026.
Albina Vision Trust's current leadership and Rose Quarter plans, and the 2027 Vanport Mosaic Festival dates.
Portland Gear's current status and whether it holds or has held a Blazers license.
The date of the 2027 Rose Festival Grand Floral Parade.
Whether the Moda Center renovation includes a local-art or heritage program that a uniform or court story could join.
